This petition filed by the petitioners who are respondent Nos.2 to 7 before the Magistrate filed under section 482 of CR.P.C for quashing proceedings in Crl.Misc.57/2022 on the file of MMTC III,
Bengaluru filed by the respondent under section 12 of Protection of Women's from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (herein after referred as DV Act).

2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent.
3. The case of the petitioner is that the respondent No.1 was married to the son of the petitioner No.1 and their marriage was held on 07.12.2017.

Subsequently, they said to have gone to Dubai on Smt Tasleem Unnisa vs Smt Neha Sultana on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24994525/
2 01.02.2018 and later the respondents are said to have harassed the respondent physically and mentally and demanded dowry.

sentences.text: Therefore, she has already filed a complaint against these petitioners and husband for the offences punishable under section 498A of IPC and other offences in Crime No.151/2019 before the Basavanagudi Police, she also filed petition before the MMTC Court under DV Act, seeking for various reliefes, which is under challenge.
4. The learned counsel for petitioner contended that the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the parents-in-law, petitioner Nos.3, 5 and 6 are the daughters of the petitioner No.1.
The petitioner No.4 is the husband of petitioner No.3, they are all family members and in-laws, who are all falsely implicated by the respondent.
Therefore, it is contended that there is no shared house and they have not at all lived together with the respondent Nos.2 and her husband.
Further submits, the respondent never stayed at Mysore, but she was residing at Bangalore along with her husband.

Therefore, question of filing the complaint against the petitioners under the DV Act, does not arise,
it is abuse of process of law.
Hence, prayed for quashing the proceedings.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent strenuously objected the petition and contented that the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are none other than the close relative of the father of respondent.
The petitioner No.1 is sister of respondent's father and marriage was held within the close relatives of the respondent.
All these petitioners are residing at one address at Mysore and they are residing in one roof of the house at Mysore.
Further contented that, after the marriage both husband and wife went to Dubai, for which the father of respondent had paid Rs.2,00,000/-.
Subsequently, there was continuous harassment from the petitioner's family.
The dowry articles, huge gold, cash and other articles were within the custody of all these petitioners.
They had withheld the articles and did not return the same.
The golden ornaments brought by the respondent has been pledged by petitioner No.1 and given money to her son-in-law for doing business i.e., to the petitioner No.4.
All the household materials given at the time of marriage, including gold and silver articles are within the custody of these petitioners.

The respondents sought direction from the trial Court to direct these petitioners to return the golden ornaments, household articles, from these petitioners, apart from compensation including maintenance for her.
Therefore, in order to direct these petitioners to return back the golden ornaments, cash and other materials, these petitioners are necessary before the trial court.
Further contended that their identity are not disputed, therefore they need not appear before the Court regularly and therefore prayed for dismissing petition.

6. Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for parties and perused the records, it is not in dispute the marriage of the respondent was performed with the son of the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 which was held in the year December 2017.
The respondent and her husband went to Dubai and thereafter both of them returned.
The allegation is from the family of respondent, the accused persons were demanding and received Rs.2,00,000/- for traveling to abroad searching for job and the same was given.

At the time of marriage, there was demand and acceptance of dowry ornaments,
cash, golden ornaments etc., was there.
It is also an admitted fact, the respondent already filed complaint to the police which is registered in Crime No.151/2019 by the Basavanagudi police station.
The learned counsel for respondent submits the respondent had stayed in the house of the petitioners at Mysore, until she was thrown out by the petitioners.

Therefore, it is contended that merely because a criminal case has been registered against these petitioners, a DV proceedings Smt Tasleem Unnisa vs Smt Neha Sultana on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24994525/
3 cannot be quashed.

sentences.text: Admittedly, there are no documents to show from the petitioners, that the petitioners returned all the dowry articles, including gold, silver and household utensils, apart from cash to the respondent family but they are holding the same.
A pawn receipt produced by the respondent counsel reveals, that the petitioner No.1 had pledged the golden ornaments of the respondent with a pawn broker and received Rs.20,000/-.
It is alleged that the said amount has been given to her son-in-law/petitioner No.4, for doing business and there are so many golden ornaments which has been pledged and sold by the petitioners.

Therefore, it is contended that in order to recover those ornaments, cash, and other dowry articles these petitioners are necessary,
before the Magistrate.
Considering the facts and circumstances of case, though for some time the petitioner's son and the respondent had stayed in Dubai.

The main allegation goes that all these accused persons had demanded further dowry and had received cash of Rs.2,00,000/- subsequent to the marriage and all the golden ornaments and other dowry articles are still in the house of petitioners at Mysore.
Of course, the respondent had chosen to file complaint at Bangalore and DV Act case also filed before Bangalore court.
Only because the petitioners are residing at Mysore and not at Bangalore, that itself is not ground to say that they are not necessary parties, before the Court.
Even otherwise, the police complaint under section 498A of IPC, which is pending before the court that itself is not a ground to quash these DV Act proceedings.
It is altogether different from the 498A of IPC case, for getting the shared house, compensation, maintenance and other directions for returning of the dowry articles.
Therefore, the respondent can also maintain a DV Act proceedings paralelly along with criminal proceedings filed under section 498A of IPC.
Therefore, the contention of the petitioners cannot be acceptable and a parallel proceedings can be quashed.
On the other hand, this petitioner withheld all the dowry articles, cash, etc.,
Therefore, in order to give the direction to these petitioners, they have to be present for the proceedings before the Magistrate under the DV Act.
Therefore, I am of the view, the petition is devoid of merits and liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.

However, the trial court is directed to exempt the regular personal appearance of the respondents before the proceedings, as the identities are not disputed and permit them to contest the matter through the advocate.
